input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: The MFN here runs the wrong way: it binds us (Customer), not Vendor. It is open-ended — every "more favourable commercial offer" we receive, with no product limitation, no time limit, and no reasonable-comparison carve-outs — so it fails the fallback (MFN limited to a defined product, 12 months, with carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory. It also requires disclosure of third-party pricing, which raises confidentiality and antitrust exposure, and it directly contradicts § 12.3 (p0044), where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. Redline deletes the obligation; any Vendor-granted MFN in our favour would remain acceptable.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted this clause: it is an open-ended most-favoured-nation obligation running against us, requiring us to disclose and match for Vendor any better third-party offer. Our playbook does not accept MFN obligations on the customer, and this also conflicts with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.
proposal.summary: Delete customer-side MFN / match-third-party-offer obligation in § 7.2.
